quote: Signature sweets are served in wheat-based monaka wafers and dorayaki; no gluten-free handling or allergen control is documented for the shared sweets kitchen.
found: The cited article says only 「手作りの最中やどら焼きにサンドして食べるのが「茶ゆ」流の食べ方なんですよ〜。」 and 「竹炭を配合して仕上げた香ばしい最中」 — it never calls the monaka wheat-based and says nothing about allergen handling. The shop's OWN site contradicts the claim outright: 東山アイスもなか is described as 「特注型で一枚毎に職人が手焼き、原材料に北陸産もち米のみを用いた最中種は自然な甘みと香ばしい風味が特徴のグルテンフリー。」 and every gelato flavour carries a printed 「アレルギー原材料」 line.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited URL; then plain fetch of the operator's own site http://chayu.info/ (iPhone UA) for the menu and allergen text
note: FALSE WARNING. 最中種 is glutinous rice, not wheat, and the shop says so in the word グルテンフリー; warabi mochi named in gf_detail is also not wheat. Only どら焼き / チョコどら and the 金沢おでんカレーパン are wheat. Rewrite the detail to name the wheat items instead of the rice ones, and drop 'no allergen control is documented' — the shop publishes per-flavour allergens.

quote: The shop centers on dairy gelato made with Noto/Ishikawa milk; sorbets and gelato are likely scooped and prepared with shared equipment, so dairy cross-contact for plant-based diners is not addressed.
found: The cited article never mentions milk at all — the closest line is 「奥能登の自然素材の美味しさが凝縮」. The milk-sourcing claim is true and is on the shop's own site: 「牧草地は自家製完熟堆肥により投入し健全な牧草の育成、牛に優しい管理をしている奥能登八戸の限定した酪農家からの生乳を使用しています。」 and 「奥能登八戸限定酪農家生乳の生乳をベースに…」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited URL, then the operator's own site
note: Repoint to http://chayu.info/ (厳選素材 section). Note the 'shared equipment' half is an inference documented by neither page — the shop's flavour list actually shows the reverse signal: every dairy flavour prints アレルギー原材料：乳 while 能登柳田ブルーベリー・ソルベ prints no allergen line at all.

quote: Fruit sorbets such as Noto Yanagida blueberry and seasonal Kanazawa watermelon are listed as plant-based flavors, giving non-dairy diners at least some options.
found: Blueberry half IS verbatim on the page: 「無農薬の新鮮なブルーベリーのみを使ったソルベは、甘酸っぱくて後味さっぱり！」 (「能登柳田ブルーベリー (ソルベ)」450円). The watermelon half is contradicted on the same page: 「金沢すいか」(450円) は「すいかの瑞々しさをぎゅっと詰め込んだ…爽やかなジェラートです」 — printed as ジェラート, not ソルベ, and served 「求肥のもっちりとした弾力が…」. The shop's own flavour list confirms only 能登柳田ブルーベリー・ソルベ has no 乳 allergen line.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited URL, cross-checked against http://chayu.info/ flavour list
note: FALSE ASSURANCE risk: 金沢すいか is a gelato on this shop's dairy base, not a sorbet. Keep 能登柳田ブルーベリー・ソルベ as the plant-based example and delete the watermelon; the shop rotates 12 flavours so a vegan must check the 乳 line on the day.

why: options — the operator states in its own words that its signature item's wafer is gluten-free: 東山アイスもなか 「原材料に北陸産もち米のみを用いた最中種は自然な甘みと香ばしい風味が特徴のグルテンフリー」, and it publishes an アレルギー原材料 line for every gelato flavour, of which exactly one (金沢大野醤油＆焦がしキャラメル: 乳/卵/大豆/小麦) contains 小麦. 雪見アイスもなか is 最中種＋求肥＋粒餡 and the 2F menu is わらび餅・あんみつ・寒天・餡子 — all rice/agar/bean. Not 'high': どら焼き/チョコどら生地 and the deep-fried 金沢おでんカレーパン are made and handled in the same small shop, and no cross-contact protocol is published. But 'no' is wrong in the dangerous direction — it warns a celiac off a shop that labels its allergens and sells a rice-wafer signature.

found: 「離れのお部屋は一名様から二〇名様まで承っております。」 and, in the cancellation policy, 「人数、内容の変更は三日前の正午までにご連絡お願い致します。」 — the ryotei explicitly takes changes to the CONTENT of a booked meal up to noon three days ahead.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited URL
note: Supported, and stronger than the record credits: 内容の変更 is a documented mechanism for a dietary request, not just an inference from private-room service.

why: ask — the record is internally inconsistent: it awards vegan_status 'ask' on the reasoning that 'a plant-based course might be arranged if requested well ahead', then awards gf_confidence 'no' on exactly the same facts. The page documents the mechanism for both — 「離れのお部屋は一名様から二〇名様まで承っております」 and 「人数、内容の変更は三日前の正午までにご連絡お願い致します」 — a made-to-order kaiseki in a detached private room that accepts content changes three days out. 'ask' is the correct tier for a place with no GF programme but a real advance-request channel; 'no' should be reserved for kitchens where the answer cannot change. Not higher than 'ask': no allergen information is published anywhere on the site, soy-sauce preparations (土佐煮, 柚庵焼き) are on the standard bento, and /news/ advertises お座敷天婦羅.
